qa_pairs.question: How do you request a full NVIDIA H100 GPU for a compute job on the Nibi cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: To request a full H100-80gb GPU on the Nibi cluster, you can use the Slurm option `--gpus=h100:1` or `--gpus=h100_80gb:1` for a single GPU. For multiple H100-80gb GPUs per node, use options like `--gpus-per-node=h100:2`, `--gpus-per-node=h100:3`, or `--gpus-per-node=h100:4`. To request multiple full H100 GPUs spread anywhere, use `--gpus=h100:n`, replacing 'n' with the total number of GPUs desired.

qa_pairs.question: What are the available Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) sizes on the Nibi cluster and their specifications?
qa_pairs.answer: Approximately half of the GPU nodes on the Nibi cluster are configured with Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, offering three instance sizes: H100-1g.10gb, which provides 1/8th of the computing power with 10GB of GPU memory; H100-2g.20gb, offering 2/8th of the computing power with 20GB of GPU memory; and H100-3g.40gb, providing 3/8th of the computing power with 40GB of GPU memory.

qa_pairs.question: How do you request a single specific Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) instance for a compute job on the Nibi cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: To request one specific Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) instance for your compute job on the Nibi cluster, use the corresponding Slurm option: for an H100-1g.10gb instance, use `--gpus=h100_1g.10gb:1`; for an H100-2g.20gb instance, use `--gpus=h100_2g.20gb:1`; and for an H100-3g.40gb instance, use `--gpus=h100_3g.40gb:1`.
